name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,231

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Furious driver called out Gaitskell’s initial and forename

indicators.note: something called out is spoken, so the solver writes down what the pieces sound like rather than how they look

blocks.note: the first letter of Gaitskell is G, said as 'gee'
the Labour leader Gaitskell's first name was Hugh

explanation.surface: A road-rage motorist shouts out the name and initial of the old Labour leader Hugh Gaitskell.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Gaitskell led Britain's Labour Party in the 1950s. Said aloud, 'G Hugh' is JEHU.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Kings, Jehu drove his chariot furiously, so the name became a jocular word for any reckless coachman or motorist.

clue.text: Australian bluebottle bound to be under dunny?

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting under something means following it, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a dunny is Australian slang for a toilet; john is another slang word for one
to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: An Australian blowfly is sure to be found buzzing beneath the outdoor toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The bluebottle looks like a fly, but it is old slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform. JOHN HOP is Australian rhyming slang for cop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a dated slang term for a police officer, and Australians call a cop a John Hop in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Holy order’s private teasing in Powys town

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters go inside the second

blocks.note: Hay-on-Wye, the book town in Powys, Wales, is often called simply Hay
a GI is an American private soldier
arch means playfully mischievous or teasing

explanation.surface: A religious order's soldier is being teased in a Welsh market town.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY holds GI and ARCH. Powys is a county in Wales, and Hay-on-Wye is its famous town of bookshops.
explanation.definitionFit: A hagiarchy is rule by saints or holy men, or an order of such persons, so it is a sacred hierarchy.

clue.text: Bouquet’s “triple essence” in mineral water for syrup producer

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, and triple asks for three letters taken from the very centre
placed in something else means these letters sit inside the other word

blocks.note: Perrier is a French brand of sparkling mineral water
the three central letters of the seven-letter word bouquet

explanation.surface: A perfume's concentrated essence is added to bottled water to flavour a syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup is Cockney rhyming slang: syrup of figs, wig. So a syrup producer is a wigmaker, not a confectioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A perruquier is a maker of wigs, and syrup is British rhyming slang for a wig, so this is the producer of them.

clue.text: Drink or drugs nearly filling each Madeira maturation chamber

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
a filling sits inside something, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: ea is the standard abbreviation for each
stuff is slang for both alcohol and illicit drugs

explanation.surface: Alcohol or narcotics are hidden in every cellar where Madeira wine ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An estufa is the heated room or store in which Madeira wine is warmed to age it, a technical term from the Portuguese for stove.

clue.text: Gunners called up approve final battle

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
called someone on the phone, rang them
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Artillerymen are summoned to sign off on a last decisive engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology Ragnarok is the doom of the gods, the last great battle at the end of the world.

clue.text: Like mercury and potassium, metallic element is found in most of savoury tart

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
things found in something are inside it, so these pieces sit within the other word

blocks.note: a quiche is a savoury egg tart
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
silver is a metallic element
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: mercury, potassium and a metal are discovered baked inside a savoury tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the old name for the liquid metal mercury, so quicksilverish describes something resembling it, quick and shifting.

clue.text: Compound that complements you and yours?

indicators.note: complementing each word means supplying its partner pronoun from the other side of a conversation

blocks.note: the first-person counterpart of the second-person pronoun
the first-person possessive matching the second-person one

explanation.surface: A riddle about a thing that completes both you and what belongs to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a compliment, but each pronoun is swapped for its opposite number in the I and you pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An imine is an organic chemical compound containing a carbon-nitrogen double bond, related to the amines.

clue.text: Small type protecting French from the person who’s uncivil to the Bard

definitions.text: the person who’s uncivil to the Bard

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it, so these letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: ruby is an old printers' name for a small type size, five and a half point
des is French for 'of the' or 'from the'

explanation.surface: A small-print notice shields French speakers from someone who insults Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare; the definition says the word is his, an archaic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudesby is a Shakespearean word for an insolent, ill-mannered fellow, used in Twelfth Night and The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Glow of reddish-purple around radioactive ring basically knocking out nurse

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it, so these letters are split to hold the next pieces
knocking something out removes it, so those letters are taken away from the word before

blocks.note: plum is a dark reddish-purple colour
hot is slang for radioactive
the letter O is ring-shaped
basically means in essence
SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A purple glow surrounds a radioactive ring, which basically knocks the nurse out.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUM holds HOT and O; 'in essence' minus SEN leaves INESCE. Puce is the colour that springs to mind first, but its U never fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To photoluminesce is to emit light after absorbing light, a kind of glowing seen in fluorescent materials.

clue.text: Supposedly superior part of Ginger Baker’s kit

blocks.note: first meaning: snobbish, putting on airs
second meaning: the pair of foot-operated cymbals in a drum kit

explanation.walkthrough: Ginger Baker was the drummer of the rock band Cream; his kit is a drum kit. 'Part of' looks like a hidden-word signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: High-hat is both an adjective for a haughty, supercilious manner and a variant spelling of the hi-hat cymbal pair on a drum kit.

clue.text: Within range, land one type of whitefish

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed within the other word, inside its outer letters

blocks.note: to gad is to range or roam about
to land a prize is to win it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An angler on a long stretch of water lands a particular kind of whitefish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gwiniad is a whitefish found in Bala Lake in Wales, its name from the Welsh for white.

clue.text: Book date for dancing in Torchwood captain’s embrace

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and rearrange themselves into a new order
being in someone's embrace means sitting inside their arms, so these letters go inside
an embrace wraps around, so the name surrounds the shuffled letters

blocks.note: Captain Jack Harkness leads the team in the BBC science-fiction series Torchwood
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinner date at which you dance in the arms of a dashing TV captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Torchwood is a BBC spin-off of Doctor Who; its captain is Jack Harkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart of Darkness is Joseph Conrad's 1899 novella about a voyage up the Congo River, a celebrated literary work.

clue.text: From Scotland, a little deer trophy is brought back

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: an elk is a large deer
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A hunter returns from the Scottish Highlands with a small deer's head as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Puckle is a Scots word meaning a small quantity or a few, so a Scottish way of saying a bit.

clue.text: Briefly visit crow and parrot

blocks.note: to pop in is to make a short visit
the jay is a member of the crow family

explanation.surface: A quick visit from two birds, a crow and a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Popinjay is an old word for a parrot, now mostly used of a vain, gaudily dressed person who chatters.

clue.text: Monkeys with Judge and impeaches, involving leader of House

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
involving something means taking it inside, so a letter is wrapped within the word

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
to impeach is to accuse formally
the first letter of house

explanation.surface: A judge brings impeachment charges against primates, starting with the Speaker of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacchus is an old name for the common marmoset, so jacchuses are those small South American monkeys.

clue.text: Nothing for Gainsbourg in piano groove for Kind of Blue?

indicators.note: placed in something means these letters sit inside the other word

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a rut is a groove worn in a road
Serge Gainsbourg was French, and rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A music quiz linking Serge Gainsbourg, a piano groove and Miles Davis's album Kind of Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind of Blue is the famous Miles Davis jazz album, but here blue means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in British usage means indecent or risqué, and prurient means having an unhealthy interest in sexual matters.

clue.text: Time to follow brilliant Arabian man, the first man in Middle Eastern religion

definitions.text: the first man in Middle Eastern religion

indicators.note: this piece is told to come after the others, so it is placed at the end

blocks.note: gay in its older sense of bright and showy
Omar is a common Arabic man's name
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dazzling Arab is the original human in a Middle Eastern faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Gayomart is the primeval human of Zoroastrian mythology, the Persian faith's counterpart to Adam.

clue.text: Water coolers with stemmed cups for ventriloquists?

indicators.note: a ventriloquist cannot move the lips for a B, so a G is said in its place, as in 'gottle of geer'

blocks.note: goblets are drinking cups on a stem

explanation.surface: Water jugs come with a set of wine glasses for the puppet act.
explanation.walkthrough: The ventriloquist's 'gottle of geer' for 'bottle of beer' is the joke: B turns to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A goglet is a long-necked porous earthenware jar used in hot countries to keep drinking water cool by evaporation.

clue.text: Turns out stone cold, the writer’s recalled

indicators.note: recalled things are called back, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the writer is the setter, I, and the writer's is I have, contracted

explanation.surface: A writer remembers how the stone turned out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's means I've, the contraction of I have, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone out is to expel them from their home, which is exactly what a landlord does when he evicts tenants.

clue.text: Possible effect of barber’s rash evacuation of Scilly (and one of Dodecanese) Isles

indicators.note: evacuating a word empties out its insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Scilly
Cos, or Kos, is one of the Dodecanese islands of Greece
the first and last letters of Isles

explanation.surface: A hasty evacuation of the Isles of Scilly and a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isles of Scilly lie off Cornwall. 'Rash' looks like an adjective for the evacuation but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycosis is an inflammation of the hair follicles of the beard, also called barber's itch, which a careless shave can bring on.

clue.text: Ginger’s family has Em, I’m excluded from vocal set

indicators.note: things excluded from a set are left out of it, so those letters go

blocks.note: each of the five vowels, A, E, I, O and U, paired with M in turn
taken as written: two members of that set

explanation.surface: A singer called Em is left out of a family's vocal group.
explanation.walkthrough: The set runs AM, EM, IM, OM, UM; with EM and IM gone, three are left.
explanation.definitionFit: Amomum is a genus of aromatic plants in the ginger family, Zingiberaceae, which includes some cardamoms.

clue.text: Lay out morning hard copy with mixed sex features

indicators.note: laying things out spreads them in a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor arranges the morning's printed pages, which carry features on mixed-sex topics.
explanation.definitionFit: A gynandromorph is an organism, often an insect, with both male and female characteristics in different parts of its body.

clue.text: Small lump, not the last on Edmund Spenser’s pate

indicators.note: the last on a word is its final letter
not means without, so the chosen letter is removed

blocks.note: a nodule is a small rounded lump
the final letter of Edmund

explanation.surface: A small bump, not the most recent one, on the head of the poet Edmund Spenser.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund looks like part of the poet's name in the definition, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Noule is Spenser's spelling of noll, an archaic word for the crown or top of the head.

clue.text: Madame’s shattered record at university, it’s clear to me

indicators.note: being at a place puts one item right next to the other in sequence

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
U is the abbreviation for university
'I see' is what you say when something becomes clear

explanation.surface: A woman is devastated that her record at university is so plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame signals French, and a woman, so the feminine form with its extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: Épuisée is French for exhausted in the feminine, and shattered is British slang for utterly worn out.

clue.text: Bad applications with disadvantages, making all poles the same

indicators.note: the compass poles are N and S, and making them all alike turns the north letter into the south one

blocks.note: minuses are drawbacks or disadvantages

explanation.surface: Poor job applications have drawbacks, putting every candidate from Poland on an equal footing.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles look like people from Poland, but they are the magnetic poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuses are wrong or improper uses of something, so they are bad applications of it.

clue.text: Too funny, in Beadle’s name, having head replaced by stone mason’s art

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into a strange new order
the head of a word is its first letter, and it is swapped for what follows
placed in a name means these letters go inside it

blocks.note: Jeremy Beadle was a British TV presenter famous for hidden-camera pranks
st is the abbreviation for stone
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prankster's jokes, too funny, are made in Jeremy Beadle's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Beadle's name is his first name, not the surname printed. The swapped head and the inserted letters both act on that first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereotomy is the art or technique of cutting solids, especially stone blocks, into shapes for building.

clue.text: Some of Plato’s characters, steeped in solipsism

indicators.note: something steeped in a liquid is immersed in it, so the letters sit concealed inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Some of the figures in Plato's dialogues are absorbed in solipsism.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters suggests the people in Plato's dialogues, but here they are letters of the Greek alphabet he wrote in.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so psis are some of the written characters Plato would have used.
